rules.name: Fake countdown timer
rules.description: Artificial countdown timer creates false urgency and pressures users into hasty purchase decisions before they can research alternatives.

rules.name: Stock scarcity manipulation
rules.description: Exaggerated or fake low-stock warnings trigger FOMO and prevent users from taking time to make a rational decision.

rules.name: Fake social proof urgency
rules.description: Fabricated viewer counts like '19 people are viewing this now' manufacture false competition to pressure the user into buying.

rules.name: Aggressive urgency copy
rules.description: Repeated urgency language across the page is designed to override calm, rational decision-making and force a faster purchase.

rules.name: Confirm shaming
rules.description: Opt-out text is deliberately written to shame or guilt users for declining an offer, exploiting social psychology against the user.

rules.name: Hidden auto-renewal
rules.description: Subscription auto-renewal terms are deliberately buried in small print. Easy to sign up — nearly impossible to notice before being charged.

rules.name: Forced continuity
rules.description: Free trials silently convert to paid subscriptions. Cancellation is buried behind phone calls or sent letters to discourage users.

rules.name: Trick cancellation flow
rules.description: Cancellation is routed through high-friction channels like phone calls or physical mail to maximise subscription retention by making it painful.

rules.name: Hidden processing fee
rules.description: Extra fees are only revealed at the final checkout step, after the user has already invested time selecting products and entering details.

rules.name: Pre-ticked opt-in checkbox
rules.description: Checkboxes are pre-selected for marketing subscriptions or data sharing that the user never explicitly chose. The user must actively opt out.

rules.name: Privacy zuckering
rules.description: Vague consent language is engineered to extract maximum data permissions without the user genuinely understanding what they are agreeing to.

rules.name: Disguised advertisement
rules.description: Paid placements are styled to look identical to organic results. Users cannot tell what is an ad and what is genuine content.

rules.name: Misdirection urgency copy
rules.description: Scattered urgency phrases across the entire page are used to maintain constant psychological pressure throughout the browsing session.

rules.name: Bait and switch
rules.description: User is attracted by one price or offer but is redirected to a more expensive option at the time of purchase.
keywords: no longer available at this price

rules.name: Facebook tracking pixel
rules.description: The Meta Pixel records every page visit and purchase and links it to Facebook user profiles. Requires explicit opt-in consent under GDPR.

rules.name: Google Analytics tracking
rules.description: Google Analytics transmits user behaviour data and IP address to Google. Requires a valid Consent Management Platform under GDPR in EU.

rules.name: Hotjar session recording
rules.description: Hotjar records mouse movements, clicks, scrolls, and keystrokes including form inputs as video replays. Requires explicit user consent.

rules.name: Missing cookie consent
rules.description: No cookie consent banner or Consent Management Platform detected. Setting tracking cookies without prior consent is a GDPR violation — fines up to 20 million euros.
